facts.text: Field monitoring, also called operational or in-service monitoring, is the planned collection and review of data from machines in real use after release to check behavior against safety-case predictions and catch problems missed by tests.
facts.quote: Field monitoring, also called operational or in-service monitoring, is the planned collection and review of data from machines in real use after release

facts.text: The field-monitoring plan specifies recording on every machine each intervention and whether it was correct, unnecessary or ambiguous; near misses and known misses; sensor health; time in degraded mode; operator overrides and switch-offs; and weather, light, site and task conditions.
facts.quote: each intervention and whether it was correct, unnecessary or ambiguous; near misses and known misses; sensor health; time in degraded mode; operator overrides and switch-offs; and the conditions (weather, light, site, task)

facts.text: Field-monitoring rates are reported per operating hour and reviewed on a fixed cadence.
facts.quote: Rates are reported per operating hour, reviewed on a fixed cadence

facts.text: Field-monitoring results are fed back into models and the scenario catalog and tied to triggers for widening or narrowing the operating domain.
facts.quote: fed back into the models and the scenario catalog, and tied to triggers for widening or narrowing the operating domain

facts.text: Field monitoring observes a live safety function, whereas shadow mode disables the brake and logs only decisions.
facts.quote: It differs from shadow mode: there the brake is disabled and only the decisions are logged; here the function is live.

facts.text: The documented program's fourth step is “release in stages with field monitoring,” monitoring misses and nuisance brakes and feeding new field scenarios back to the start of the process.
facts.quote: the fourth step of the documented program structure, "release in stages with field monitoring", with misses and nuisance brakes monitored and new field scenarios flowing back to the start of the process [Chapter 1]

facts.text: Evidence on durability, sensor aging and contamination relies on monitoring after release.
facts.quote: Durability, sensor aging and contamination rely on monitoring after release [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The South African specification's final readiness level calls for statistical monitoring in production over an extended period, with 3 months or 2000 hours given as examples.
facts.quote: The South African specification's final readiness level calls for statistical monitoring in production over "an extended period (e.g., 3 months or 2000 hours)"

facts.text: The South African specification requires logging at 10 hertz during interventions, with records retained for 7 days on board and 3 months on a server.
facts.quote: requires logging at 10 hertz during interventions, kept 7 days on board and 3 months on a server [Chapters 3, 7]

facts.text: In-service monitoring is the fifth pillar of the United Nations assessment method for automated driving.
facts.quote: In-service monitoring is the fifth pillar of the United Nations assessment method for automated driving

facts.text: The booklet judges in-service monitoring to be the only route to close dust and glare model gaps over time.
facts.quote: in the booklet's judgment, "the only route to close the dust and glare model gaps over time" [Chapter 10]

facts.text: Operator behavior changes after a technology is introduced, and only field time reveals those changes.
facts.quote: Operator behavior changes after a technology is introduced, and only field time reveals it [Chapter 1].

facts.text: A four-month validation window cannot sample all seasons, rare events or operator adaptation.
facts.quote: A four-month window cannot sample all seasons, rare events or operator adaptation.

facts.text: Field monitoring allows evidence to keep growing after release and makes staged release a legitimate safety strategy rather than merely a way to ship early.
facts.quote: Monitoring is how the evidence keeps growing after release, and it is what makes staged release a legitimate safety strategy rather than a way to ship early.
